description:
FILED s377 (Fable ruling on s376 Ask 4, docs/fable-answers-s376.md §4). Residue of #276: the EMPTY `{}` case is now fixed (perl decides it on the next character, no ambiguity), but the ambiguous shapes `f {$k, $v}` and `f {%h}` after a paren-less list operator are still parsed as BLOCKS where perl's toke.c intuit_curly reads hash constructors. SILENT-WRONG family: the call's argument count changes with no diagnostic.

DO NOT build until a real cause line (sweep / board / CPAN) names it — s376 found none in any population. When built, the bar is matching toke.c's ACTUAL intuit_curly rule (not a guessed heuristic), with the breaking-case population measured first (feedback_probe_the_breaking_case). The one term-position site is PExpr's Block arm where _block_is_hash_constructor/_block_is_empty are consulted (Pl/PExpr.pm ~line 490).

SECOND POPULATION, MEASURED s396: the FOREACH LIST, not just a call argument.

    for my $r ({5,6},{7,8}) { push @o, ref($r) }
    perl: "HASH HASH"    PCL: "  HASH"  (three iterations, first two empty)

The FIRST element only: PCL flattens the leading `{5,6}` to a list and reads
only the second brace group as a hash constructor.  Same cause (the ambiguous
brace after a construct that can take either), different position.  Found while
probing #327 (`for \my %h ({5,6},{7,8})`, op/lvref.t line 359) -- so this file
now has a cause line: op/lvref.t needs it, once #314 family F-F unblocks the
file.  A key=>value spelling (`{a=>5}`) is unambiguous and works.
subject: DEFERRED (#191 pattern): `f {$k, $v}` / `f {%h}` in term position — perl's intuit_curly reads hash constructor, PCL reads block
